clue.text: Mr Jorrocks's hunt is mostly held close to Sowerby Bridge

indicators.note: most of the word, so its final letter is left off

parts.note: handled, as in held in the hands

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: its close, the final letter, is taken
to bridge a gap is to cross it

explanation.surface: A huntsman's pack is said to be kept near a small town in West Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Sowerby Bridge is a real Yorkshire town, so the two words read as one name; they are split here. Handley Cross is R. S. Surtees's comic hunting novel.
explanation.definitionFit: In Surtees's novel the grocer John Jorrocks becomes Master of the Handley Cross foxhounds, the hunt that gives the book its title.

clue.text: Eliot claimed to show fear in this novel

definitions.text: Eliot claimed to show fear in this novel

parts.note: The Waste Land promises to show the reader fear in a famous four-word phrase
Evelyn Waugh took that phrase as the title of his novel

explanation.walkthrough: T. S. Eliot's line is 'I will show you fear in a handful of dust'; Waugh borrowed the last words for his 1934 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel by Evelyn Waugh takes its title from the very line of Eliot's poem in which fear is shown.

clue.text: What helps when looking up Anne Shirley's friend, Barry?

indicators.note: in a down entry, looking up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: something that helps is an aid

explanation.surface: A question about what helps when consulting a reference for a character in Anne of Green Gables.
explanation.definitionFit: In L. M. Montgomery's Anne of Green Gables, the heroine's bosom friend is the girl Diana Barry.

clue.text: Writers' bureaux regularly receive stories in redraft

indicators.note: a redraft rearranges the text, so the letters are mixed together
taking every other letter of the following word, starting from its first

parts.note: every other letter of this word is kept
taken as written, ready to be redrafted

explanation.surface: Desks at a writers' agency take in tales that need rewriting.
explanation.definitionFit: An escritoire is a writing desk, and bureau is another name for that piece of furniture.

clue.text: The line following "For whom the bell tolls"

definitions.text: The line following "For whom the bell tolls"

parts.note: seems to mean the next line of a text, but is a procession of people following
seems to quote Donne or Hemingway, but is the dead person at a funeral

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation suggests asking for the next line of Donne's meditation; the line is instead the mourners walking behind the coffin of the person the bell is tolled for.
explanation.definitionFit: A cortege is a solemn funeral procession, the line of mourners walking behind a coffin.

clue.text: See 16
Most thin yarns can tie storage boxes

indicators.note: the words box up the answer, holding it inside them

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of yarns, through can and tie, into the start of storage

explanation.surface: Fine threads are used to fasten storage boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarns' and 'boxes' read as the things being tied; boxes is the verb that encloses the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scantiest is the superlative of scanty, meaning meagre or barely sufficient, so it means thinnest.

clue.text: An agent on marihuana crashed when collecting a vehicle

indicators.note: collecting takes something in, so one part is placed inside the other
something crashed is wrecked, so these letters are smashed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be crashed into a new order
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A spy high on drugs had a car accident while picking up a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene's novel is about a vacuum-cleaner salesman recruited as a British secret agent in Cuba.

clue.text: A talk about Olaf Kyrre?

indicators.note: turned about, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
gas is idle talk

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a lecture on an eleventh-century Norwegian king.
explanation.walkthrough: Olaf Kyrre was king of Norway; his story is told in the Heimskringla, so the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The reign of Olaf the Peaceful is recounted as one of the Norse kings' sagas, a medieval prose narrative.

clue.text: Not exactly a consul or one who aimed to become one

definitions.note: a person who sought to be a consul

indicators.note: the letters are not exactly as written but rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is not quite a consul, or else only aspired to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'one' is the numeral; the second points back to consul.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's tragedy the Roman general Caius Marcius Coriolanus stands for election to the consulship and is rejected by the people.

clue.text: Glorify one town: one linked to Kent?

parts.note: Deal is a coastal town in Kent
Kent is a county in the South East of England

explanation.surface: A puzzling invitation to praise a single town tied to a southern English county.
explanation.definitionFit: To idealise someone is to regard them as perfect, so it means to exalt or glorify them.

clue.text: Tennyson had her "whirl like leaves" loudly towards one old lady

parts.note: f, forte, the musical direction to play loudly
at, as in aiming at
ma, a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A poet's heroine is pictured spinning noisily towards an elderly woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatima is a poem by Tennyson spoken by a passionate woman, who says of her lover's kisses that they make her senses whirl.

clue.text: Martins and Lime turned up in one

definitions.text: Martins and Lime turned up in one

parts.note: Holly Martins and Harry Lime, the two men of Graham Greene's The Third Man
seems to mean they appeared somewhere, but they ride round and up in a fairground attraction

explanation.walkthrough: In The Third Man the two old friends meet on the giant wheel at the Prater in Vienna; 'turned up' hints at its rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ferris wheel is a large upright revolving wheel with passenger cars, like the Vienna Riesenrad in the film.

clue.text: Borthrop's one with lots to pass on

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Borthrop Trumbull's trade in George Eliot's Middlemarch

definitions.text: one with lots to pass on
definitions.meaning: second meaning: someone who sells off items, called lots, at a sale

explanation.walkthrough: Mr Borthrop Trumbull is the long-winded seller of goods at sales in Middlemarch; 'lots' are items under the hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: An auctioneer conducts a public sale, offering numbered lots to the highest bidder.

clue.text: A description of the most unpleasant sort in The Metamorphosis

definitions.text: A description of the most unpleasant

indicators.note: a metamorphosis is a complete change of form, so these letters change their order

parts.note: taken as written, including the first word of Kafka's title

explanation.surface: Kafka's The Metamorphosis is cited for a portrait of the nastiest kind of creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Metamorphosis' looks like Kafka's title; its first word is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorniest, the superlative of thorny, describes what is most prickly, troublesome or difficult to handle.

clue.text: Chopin's rebellious wife returned with Beethoven's third

parts.note: his third letter is taken

indicators.note: sent back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: and, as in bread with butter

explanation.surface: A composer's defiant spouse comes back carrying a famous symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: Chopin here is Kate Chopin, the American novelist, not the composer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Kate Chopin's The Awakening, Edna Pontellier rebels against her marriage and the role society expects of her.

clue.text: This artist loves mingling with New York's fringe

indicators.note: the pieces are mixed together in a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O; several of them give several Os
N, the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: a fringe is the edge, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the city name; its fringe is taken

explanation.surface: A painter has romances while socialising on the edge of the New York scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoko Ono is a Japanese-born conceptual and performance artist based for decades in New York.

clue.text: Publishing more about art, but dropping an article about Romeo

parts.note: re, meaning concerning

indicators.note: placed round, so this piece goes inside the shortened word
letting fall, so the next piece is taken out

parts.note: painting is an art
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A further printing of a book on art, cut short by the omission of a love story.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Reprinting is printing again a book already issued, so a publisher is bringing out more copies.

clue.text: Posthumus's order got to him from an Italian city by satellite

parts.note: Pisan means from Pisa
Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: A message to a Shakespeare character arrives from Italy by satellite link.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places one piece beside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cymbeline, Posthumus sends his servant Pisanio a letter ordering him to murder Imogen, which Pisanio refuses to carry out.

clue.text: An academic's the subject of Bion's epitaph

parts.note: taken as written
a don is a university teacher, and 's here stands for is

explanation.surface: A scholar is named as the person a Greek poet's lament commemorates.
explanation.definitionFit: Bion of Smyrna wrote the Lament for Adonis, a funeral song mourning the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite.

clue.text: A bloomer broadcast and reproduced on the radio

parts.note: to sow seed is to broadcast it

indicators.note: heard over the air, so the word is matched by its sound

parts.note: bred, as animals do

explanation.surface: A bakery loaf, spread and copied on a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a British loaf of bread, but here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sowbread is the cyclamen, a plant whose flowers make it something that blooms.

clue.text: A note saying more cuts are needed!

definitions.note: a verb: to cut through again, as when more cuts are made

parts.note: re, the second note of the sol-fa scale
a saw is an old saying

explanation.surface: A memo announcing further budget cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: To resaw is to saw timber again, cutting it a second time into thinner pieces.

clue.text: A piece of play ultimately lacking ball control

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: lacking at the very end, so the scene word loses its last letter

parts.note: a scene is a section of a play
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A sports report notes a passage of play that, in the end, lacked control of the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball control' looks like one football phrase; ball is the dance, control the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascendance is a position of dominance or power over others, which amounts to control.

clue.text: Julius Caesar's cast

parts.note: Caesar crossing the Rubicon declared something was cast
seems to mean the actors in the play, but is what was thrown

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the actors of Shakespeare's play; Caesar's words 'alea iacta est' mean the die is cast.
explanation.definitionFit: A die is a single dice, the cube thrown in Caesar's saying about crossing the Rubicon.

clue.text: He wrote novels, but mostly plays an oboe, endlessly

definitions.text: He wrote novels, but mostly plays

indicators.note: with no end, so the instrument's name loses its final letter

parts.note: the shawm was the medieval forerunner of the oboe

explanation.surface: An author who wrote fiction but mainly performs on a woodwind instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plays' seems to be a verb for music; it is the dramas Shaw mostly wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw wrote five early novels before becoming famous as a dramatist.

clue.text: He's apparently emptied out one of Dr. Fell's cases

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read literally, a man with nothing inside him
second meaning: a John Dickson Carr novel featuring the detective Dr Gideon Fell

explanation.walkthrough: The title, also called The Three Coffins in the US, describes a man literally hollowed out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hollow Man is John Dickson Carr's 1935 novel featuring the detective Dr Gideon Fell.
